The weather of Ireland in Gladys, from [Met Éireann](https://www.met.ie/), the
Irish national meteorological service: its forecasts (the HARMONIE model
around Ireland, then ECMWF up to 10 days) and its **official weather
warnings**, county by county. Open data: **no account, no API key**.

Copyright Met Éireann, source [www.met.ie](https://www.met.ie/), data
licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
This integration is a community project, not affiliated with Met Éireann.

## What you get

- **The Gladys weather widget and the chat assistant** use Met Éireann: the
  current weather (temperature, humidity, pressure, dew point, wind and
  gusts, cloud cover, sunrise and sunset), the next 24 hours with the rain of
  each hour and its probability, and the next 8 days. Day and night have
  their own icons. Everything is shown in **°C, m/s and mm** or in **°F, mph
  and inches**, following the unit system of each Gladys user.
- **The Met Éireann warnings of your county** (yellow, orange, red: wind,
  rain, snow and ice, thunderstorms, fog, low or high temperature, coastal),
  shown as alerts on the weather widget, in force or announced. The built-in
  **weather alert** scene trigger of Gladys works with them, and fires
  within a minute of a change.
- **Scene trigger "Met Éireann warning changed"**: a warning issued,
  upgraded, downgraded, updated or lifted, with its colour and a sentence in
  your language.
- **Scene trigger "Rain or snow expected within the hour"**.
- **Scene action "Get the precipitation of the next hour"**.
- **Scene action "Get the forecast of the day"** (today or tomorrow).
- **Scene action "Get the Met Éireann warnings"**: the highest level for
  your county, to gate a scene on it.

No extra widget: the Gladys weather widget already shows the forecast and
the warnings.

**Ireland only.** Met Éireann's models cover Ireland, Northern Ireland and
the nearby seas; elsewhere there is no forecast and Gladys uses another
weather provider. The warnings cover the 26 counties of the Republic of
Ireland (Northern Ireland is covered by the Met Office). For a worldwide
forecast, install **MET Norway** instead: it covers Ireland too, but without
the Irish warnings.

## Installation

1. Check that your house has a location in Gladys: **Settings → Houses**,
   then the address or the position on the map. The integration refreshes
   the weather of every house that has one.
2. Install **Met Éireann** from the integration store (or **Integrations →
   Install from GitHub** with the address
   `https://github.com/guim31/gladys-met-eireann`). Gladys asks you to allow
   access to the location of your houses: it finds their county and watches
   the rain of the next hour.
3. Open the **Configuration** tab and click **Test Met Éireann**. The answer
   shows the current temperature of your first house and the warnings of its
   county.

That's it: the weather widget of your dashboard now shows Met Éireann. If
another weather integration is installed, pick the provider in the settings
of the weather widget.

Gladys 5.2 or later is required.

## Configuration

Nothing is mandatory.

- **County of the warnings** — **Automatic** finds the county of each house
  from its location (the nearest of about 200 Irish towns and villages).
  Choose your county yourself if your house is near a county border and the
  warnings shown are not yours. The choice applies to all your houses.
- **Units of the scene values** — the units of the temperatures, wind and
  precipitation the integration puts in scene variables. **Automatic**
  follows the unit system of the last user who looked at the weather; pick
  **Metric** or **US** to set it. The weather widget always follows each
  user's own preference.
- **Language of the scene texts** — the language of the sentences the
  integration puts in scene variables ("Orange wind warning issued for
  Kerry…"): English, French, German or Spanish. French by default;
  **Automatic** follows the language of your Gladys. The texts of Met
  Éireann itself (headline, details) are in English.

## Refresh rate and Met Éireann's terms

Met Éireann publishes its data openly and asks for a fair use of it. The
integration:

- **refreshes about every 30 minutes**, plus a few random minutes so that
  every Gladys does not call at the same second (the models run every 3 to 6
  hours);
- makes **one forecast call per house** (houses at the same place share it)
  and **one warning call** for all of them, which feed everything: the
  dashboard, the chat and the scenes. Opening the dashboard costs nothing:
  Gladys is served from the forecast in memory;
- sends coordinates rounded to 4 decimals (about 10 m) and an identification
  of the application
  (`gladys-met-eireann/<version> github.com/guim31/gladys-met-eireann`);
- pauses if Met Éireann asks to slow down (error 429) or refuses the requests
  (error 403).

During an outage, the last forecast stays visible for 3 hours at most.

## Scenes

The integration adds its cards to the scene editor, in the **Integrations**
category. The **House** field lists your houses.

### Met Éireann warning changed

Trigger: starts the scene when a warning for the county of a house is
**issued**, **upgraded** (yellow → orange…), **downgraded**, **updated**
(same level, new text or times) or **lifted** (cancelled or ended). It never
fires on the first reading after a restart, nor when Met Éireann cannot be
reached.

Optional filters (empty: everything matches):

- **House**;
- **Change**: issued, upgraded, downgraded, updated, lifted or ended;
- **Level**: yellow, orange, red;
- **Phenomenon**: wind, rain, snow and ice, thunderstorm, fog, low
  temperature, high temperature, coastal, flood, other.

Variables for the next actions: the house, the county, the change (`issued`,
`upgraded`, `downgraded`, `updated`, `lifted`), the level (`yellow`,
`orange`, `red`), the phenomenon (`wind`, `rain`, `snow`…), the headline and
the details of Met Éireann (in English), and a **summary** ready to send, for
example: "Orange wind warning issued for Kerry, from Sat 24 Oct, 14:00 to
Sun 25 Oct, 09:00."

### Rain or snow expected within the hour

Trigger: starts the scene when the hourly forecast shows precipitation this
hour or the next one, where the previous refresh showed none. It fires once
per event, at most once an hour per house, and never on the first refresh
after a restart.

Optional filters (empty: everything matches):

- **House**;
- **Precipitation**: rain, sleet or snow;
- **Intensity**: light, moderate or heavy.

Variables for the next actions: the name of the house, the kind of
precipitation (`rain`, `sleet`, `snow`), the intensity (`light`,
`moderate`, `heavy`), whether there is thunder, the minutes until it starts
(0 if it is already falling), the amount expected that hour, its probability
and a **summary** ready to send, for example: "Light rain expected in 35
minutes (60% chance)."

### Get the precipitation of the next hour

Action: tells the scene whether rain or snow is coming within the hour
(**Precipitation expected**: yes or no), when, what, how hard, and the same
summary. Leave **House** empty for your first house that has a location. If
no hourly forecast covers the hour, **Forecast available** is no: do not
read it as dry.

### Get the forecast of the day

Action: reads the forecast of **today** (the rest of the day) or
**tomorrow** for a house, and returns:

- the sky, as a Gladys code (`clear`, `partly-cloudy`, `rain`, `snow`…) and
  in words ("Rain");
- the minimum and maximum temperatures;
- the precipitation of the day and its highest probability;
- the strongest wind and the strongest gust;
- a **summary**, for example: "Tomorrow: rain, 8 to 14 °C, 5.2 mm of
  precipitation (70% chance)."

### Get the Met Éireann warnings

Action: reads the warnings of the county of a house, in force or announced,
and returns the county, whether there is at least one warning, how many, the
**highest level** (`none`, `yellow`, `orange`, `red`), whether a warning is
**in effect now**, the phenomenon and the headline of the highest one, and a
**summary**, for example: "2 Met Éireann warnings for Galway: Orange wind
warning, from Sat 24 Oct, 14:00 to Sun 25 Oct, 09:00; …". If Met Éireann
cannot be reached, or the house is outside the counties of the Republic,
**Warnings available** is no.

## Scene examples

- **Storm coming**: trigger "Met Éireann warning changed", level orange or
  red, change issued or upgraded, then a notification with the **summary**
  and the shutters closed.
- **Bring the washing in**: trigger "Rain or snow expected within the hour",
  then a notification with the **summary** variable.
- **Morning weather**: at 7:00, action "Get the forecast of the day"
  (today), then "Get the Met Éireann warnings", then a message with both
  summaries.
- **Garden watering**: every evening, action "Get the forecast of the day"
  (tomorrow), then a condition on **Precipitation** to water only when less
  than 2 mm is expected.

## Limits

- **Developed without a Gladys running in Ireland**: the integration is
  tested against real answers of Met Éireann (Dublin, Cork, Galway, and the
  warnings of Storm Boelo, October 2026). Feedback welcome.
- **Ireland and its surroundings only** (see above).
- **The county is guessed** from the nearest town: near a border, choose it
  in the configuration.
- **Warnings in English**: Met Éireann publishes them in English only; the
  integration translates the level, the phenomenon and the change, not the
  details.
- **Land warnings only**: the marine and small craft warnings are not
  included.
- **The hour is the finest step**, for about 3 days; then every 3 hours, then
  every 6 hours up to about 10 days.
- **No feels-like temperature, UV index or visibility**: the open forecast
  does not give them.
- **Today** only holds the hours still to come.
- **The days** are cut in the time zone of Gladys, for every house.
- The integration needs Gladys 5.2 or later.

## Troubleshooting

- **"No house of Gladys has a location"** — set the location of your house in
  **Settings → Houses**.
- **"Met Éireann has no usable forecast for the location of your house"** —
  the house is outside the area of Met Éireann (far from Ireland), or its
  location is wrong: check it in **Settings → Houses**.
- **"Met Éireann asks to slow down"** — too many requests from your Internet
  connection: the integration waits and retries by itself.
- **"Met Éireann refuses the requests (HTTP 403)"** — update the
  integration.
- **"Met Éireann is unreachable for now"** — Gladys cannot reach
  `openaccess.pf.api.met.ie` or `www.met.ie`: check its Internet access. The
  integration retries after 5 minutes, then less and less often.
- **The warnings are not those of my county** — choose your county in the
  configuration.
- **The dashboard still shows another provider** — open the settings of the
  weather widget and pick Met Éireann.
- **Logs**: the **Logs** tab of the integration (or `docker logs` on the
  host) shows the start, each warning change, the problems and the return of
  Met Éireann, once each. Start the container with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see
  every refresh.

## Privacy

The coordinates of your houses, rounded to about 10 m, are sent to Met
Éireann to get their forecast, and nowhere else. The warning list is the
same for everyone: its request carries no location. No account, no key,
nothing is written to disk.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Met Éireann asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nothing to sign up for | `section` | No | Met Éireann's forecasts and warnings are open data: no account, no API key. The integration refreshes the weather of every house that has a location in Gladys about every 30 minutes, and adds the warnings of its county. It covers Ireland and its surroundings only. Copyright Met Éireann, data under CC BY 4.0; this integration is not affiliated with Met Éireann. |
| County of the warnings | `select` | No | Automatic finds the county of each house from its location. Choose it yourself if your house is near a county border and the warnings shown are not yours. Applies to every house. |
| Units of the scene values | `select` | No | Units of the temperatures, wind and precipitation the integration puts in scene variables. The weather widget always follows each user's preference. |
| Language of the scene texts | `select` | No | Language of the sentences the integration puts in scene variables. Automatic follows the language of your Gladys. |

## How to install Met Éireann in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Met Éireann appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-met-eireann:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-met-eireann](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-met-eireann).

Met Éireann requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
